case_name: Arpula Ganesh vs The State Of Telangana And 3 Others

parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Telangana And 3 Others

facts_of_case: Petitioner's father was employed as Lineman and he was born out of the second marriage. His father expired while in service.

legal_principles.principle: Compassionate appointment based only on descent is impermissible.
legal_principles.held: Appointments in public service should be made strictly on the basis of open invitation of applications and comparative merit, having regard to Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India.
cited_cases: V. Sivamurthy v. State of A.P., (Year) SCC pp. 741-42, para 18

legal_principles.principle: Compassionate appointment can neither be claimed, nor be granted, unless the rules governing the service permit such appointments.
legal_principles.held: Such appointments shall be strictly in accordance with the scheme governing such appointments and against existing vacancies.
cited_cases: V. Sivamurthy v. State of A.P., (Year) SCC pp. 741-42, para 18

legal_principles.principle: There is no right to compassionate appointment; only an entitlement, where a scheme or rules envisaging it exist.
legal_principles.held: The submission which has been urged on behalf of the Union of India by the learned Additional Solicitor General is premised on the basis that there is no right as such to compassionate appointment.
cited_cases: Union of India vs. V.R.Tripathi, (Year) SCC pp. 741-42, para 18

legal_principles.principle: A scheme of compassionate appointment must have rules or a scheme which envisage such appointment.
legal_principles.held: Arpula Ganesh vs The State Of Telangana And 3 Others on 9 July, 2021
cited_cases: Union of India vs. V.R.Tripathi, (Year) SCC pp. 741-42, para 18

outcome.final_order: Direct respondent Nos.2 to 4 to consider the case of the petitioner for appointment in any eligible post on compassionate grounds

use_for_drafting: drafting a writ petition for employment on compassionate grounds
seeking appointment in eligible post under Hindu Marriage Act
challenging orders denying employment due to marital status
